For the global comparison, we projected donor expression onto ARCHIE-derived global gene embeddings using the same leave-one-chromosome-out phenotype construction applied to TransMap-gobal.
After performed genome-wide fine-mapping, each method was summarized as variant-level trans-MaxPIP annotations and evaluated using the same S-LDSC analysis.

To evaluate whether trans-QTL implicated by different scales of TransMap inform disease risk, we constructed variant-level trans-acting annotation based on the maximum posterior inclusion probability (trans-MaxPIP) from genome-wide trans-QTL fine-mapping.

For each trans-acting phenotype 𝑦, such as individual trans-eGenes, local WPC-based program scores or global sCCA-based program scores, let PIP M Y denote the PIP from finemapping of variant 𝑗 to trans-phenotype 𝑦.
Let ℋ denote the set of trans-phenotypes whose 95% CS contains variant 𝑗, we then defined with variants do not present in any credible set assigned a score of zero.
Separate trans-MaxPIP annotations were generated for TransMap-eGene, TransMap-local and TransMap-global, and analogous annotations were generated for competing methods where appropriate.
Except for the cell-type-resolved variant annotation from each scale, we also generated cross-cell-types annotations by taking maximum value of trans-MaxPIP M for variant 𝑗.

We then applied S-LDSC to quantify whether trans-acting annotations captured complex disease heritability across 57 GWAS summary statistics datasets 25 , conditioning on 53 baseline annotations comprising coding, conserved and tissue-aggregated epigenomic annotations 25, 34 (Supplementary Table 1).
text.formatted: We then applied S-LDSC to quantify whether trans-acting annotations captured complex disease heritability across 57 GWAS summary statistics datasets <ref type="bibr" target="#b24">25</ref> , conditioning on 53 baseline annotations comprising coding, conserved and tissue-aggregated epigenomic annotations <ref type="bibr" target="#b24">25,</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b33">34</ref> (Supplementary Table <ref type="table">1</ref>).

text.text: We considered two metrics, enrichment and standardized effect size, across all 57 traits, as wells as separately across the blood and brain-related traits.

Heritability enrichment quantified the concentration of trait heritability in annotated variants, whereas the standardized effect size 𝜏 ⋆ estimated the conditional informativeness of an annotation after accounting for baseline annotations and other annotations in the same model.
Joint S-LDSC models were used to test whether single-gene, local-program and global-program trans-QTL annotations carried nonredundant heritability information.
Both enrichment and 𝜏 ⋆ were estimated via a genomic block-jackknife procedure with 200 blocks that also provides standard errors.
More detailed decription of metrics can be found in Supplementary Note S6.
We constructed an xQTL-informed set of independent variants to represent common variants with prior evidence for molecular regulatory activity.
These variants were used for TransMap-global program learning and for benchmarking against competing methods, including evaluation of trans-eQTL coherence and trans-eQTL calling.

Candidate variants were assembled from multiple resources, including eQTLGen cis-and trans-eQTL 4 , MetaBrain cis-and trans-eQTL 10 , cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) protein QTL 90, 91 , and FunGen-xQTL cis-QTL across four cohorts and 77 molecular datasets 26 .
text.formatted: Candidate variants were assembled from multiple resources, including eQTLGen cis-and trans-eQTL <ref type="bibr" target="#b3">4</ref> , MetaBrain cis-and trans-eQTL <ref type="bibr" target="#b9">10</ref> , cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) protein QTL <ref type="bibr" target="#b89">90,</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b90">91</ref> , and FunGen-xQTL cis-QTL across four cohorts and 77 molecular datasets <ref type="bibr" target="#b25">26</ref> .

text.text: Candidate variants were harmonized to ROSMAP whole-genome sequencing genotypes.
We then removed duplicate variants, retained common variants with MAF ≥ 0.05, and performed LD pruning using the ROSMAP genotype reference with a pairwise 𝑟 7 < 0.1 threshold.
text.formatted: We then removed duplicate variants, retained common variants with MAF ≥ 0.05, and performed LD pruning using the ROSMAP genotype reference with a pairwise 𝑟 7 < 0.1 threshold.

text.text: This procedure yielded 43,090 approximately independent xQTL-informed variants (Supplementary Figure S1b.
text.formatted: This procedure yielded 43,090 approximately independent xQTL-informed variants (Supplementary Figure <ref type="figure" target="#fig_0">S1b</ref>.

text.text: Resourcespecific extraction rules and pipeline implementation details are provided in Supplementary Note S3.

For WPC background construction in TransMap-local, null variants were selected from genome-wide common variants, after excluding the xQTL-informed variants described above and any variants in LD with these variants (𝑟 7 > 0.1).
text.formatted: For WPC background construction in TransMap-local, null variants were selected from genome-wide common variants, after excluding the xQTL-informed variants described above and any variants in LD with these variants (𝑟 7 > 0.1).

text.text: The remaining variants were then LD-pruned to obtain 26,363 approximately independent null variants.
This design reduces enrichment of known cis-, trans-QTL and other xQTL signals in the empirical background used by WPC, while limiting redundancy among nearby correlated variants.
The resulting null set provides a regulatory-signal-depleted common variant background for estimating residual co-expression structure and calibrating WPC-based program activity comparisons.

To evaluate whether trans-eGenes or trans-ePrograms converge with downstream biomarkers through the shared genetic signals, we defined the biomarker convergence Enrichment and Recall at the colocalization event level, where each event is represented by a 95% CoS and its corresponding trait configuration.

Let 𝒞 * denote all retained 95% colocalization events considered in the analysis, 𝒞 [ denote colocalization events for trans-eGenes or trans-ePrograms, and 𝒞 \ denote colocalization events for downstream biomarkers.

Enrichment quantifies whether colocalization events involving trans-eGenes or trans-ePrograms are more likely to also involve downstream biomarker-QTL signals than expected from all colocalization events: where Enrichment > 1 indicates that downstream biomarker-QTL events occur more frequently within the specified trans-regulatory event set than expected from all retained colocalization events.
text.formatted: Enrichment quantifies whether colocalization events involving trans-eGenes or trans-ePrograms are more likely to also involve downstream biomarker-QTL signals than expected from all colocalization events: where Enrichment > 1 indicates that downstream biomarker-QTL events occur more frequently within the specified trans-regulatory event set than expected from all retained colocalization events.

text.text: Recall quantifies the fraction of downstream biomarker-QTL colocalization events that are also captured by the given trans-regulatory signal set:
For biomarker-category analyses, 𝒞 [ was defined separately for trans-eGene and trans-eProgram, whereas 𝒞 \ was restricted to events involving protein-, glycoprotein-or metabolite-QTL signals.
For cell-type analyses, 𝒞 [ and 𝒞 * were restricted to events containing the given cell type.
Statistically significant and 95% confidence intervals for Enrichment and Recall were estimated using a leave-one-chromosome-out jackknife.

To characterize the genomic context and biological interpretation of cis and trans genetic signals identified by TransMap colocalization analysis, we classified colocalization events into three regulatory categories according to their trait configurations.
A 'cis-only' colocalization event contained one or more proximal cis-eGenes without a distal trans-eGene or trans-eProgram.
A 'cis-trans' colocalization event contained at least one proximal cis-eGene and at least one distal trans-eGene or trans-eProgram.
A 'trans-only' colocalization event contained at least one distal trans-eGene or trans-eProgram without a proximal cis-eGene.

We then tested whether these categories showed distinct genomic and functional architectures by characterizing variant-level conservation 48 , gene-level loss-of-function (LoF) constraint 92 , human transcription factor (TF) 93 , and protein-protein interaction (PPI) 46 .
text.formatted: We then tested whether these categories showed distinct genomic and functional architectures by characterizing variant-level conservation <ref type="bibr" target="#b47">48</ref> , gene-level loss-of-function (LoF) constraint <ref type="bibr" target="#b91">92</ref> , human transcription factor (TF) <ref type="bibr" target="#b92">93</ref> , and protein-protein interaction (PPI) <ref type="bibr" target="#b45">46</ref> .

text.text: We used the same Enrichment across variant-, gene-and gene-gene interaction-level analyses after redefining the analysis unit and background universe.
Depending on the analysis, a unit represented a colocalized variant in 95% CoS, the gene nearest to a QTL variant, a molecular target gene, or a gene-gene interaction.
Let 𝒰 denote the background set of units, and let 𝒜, ℬ ⊆ 𝒰 denote two sets of interest.
Enrichment is defined as Enrichment(𝒜, ℬ | 𝒰) = (|𝒜 ∩ ℬ|/|𝒜|)/(|ℬ|/|𝒰|).
(i) For variant-level characterization, distance to transcription start site (TSS) was calculated from the corresponding each CoS to the nearest protein-coding gene TSS.
Variant conservation was evaluated using Zoonomia primate PhastCons scores 48 , with conserved variants defined as PhastCons > 0.9.
text.formatted: Variant conservation was evaluated using Zoonomia primate PhastCons scores <ref type="bibr" target="#b47">48</ref> , with conserved variants defined as PhastCons > 0.9.

text.text: (ii) For gene-level characterization, we distinguished two target-gene definitions.
First, nearest genes were defined as protein-coding genes closest to representative CoS and were used to characterize locus-proximal gene properties.
Second, molecular target genes were defined from the phenotypes included in the trait configuration, including proximal cis-eGenes, distal trans-eGenes and genes contributing to trans-ePrograms.
Loss-of-function-constrained genes were defined as genes with pLI > 0.9.
text.formatted: Loss-of-function-constrained genes were defined as genes with pLI > 0.9.

text.text: Human transcription factors were defined using a curated 1,631 human transcription-factor catalogue 46.
text.formatted: Human transcription factors were defined using a curated 1,631 human transcription-factor catalogue <ref type="bibr" target="#b45">46</ref>.

text.text: (iii) For gene-gene interaction characterization, the unit of analysis was a gene connection.
For cis-trans configurations, observed gene pairs were defined between proximal cis-eGenes and distal trans-eGenes or genes assigned to trans-ePrograms in the same colocalization event.
For within-trans analyses, observed gene pairs were defined among distal genes linked to the same trans-regulatory event or program.
Protein-protein interaction support was evaluated using STRINGdb 45 after mapping genes to protein-coding identifiers.
text.formatted: Protein-protein interaction support was evaluated using STRINGdb <ref type="bibr" target="#b44">45</ref> after mapping genes to protein-coding identifiers.

text.text: For AD-centered colocalization, we compared lead-variant conservation across AD-only, AD-cis, AD-trans and AD-cis-trans events using two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum tests 94 , where the lead variant was the highest-VCP variant in each 95% CoS (or the highest-PIP variant from AD fine-mapping for AD-only loci).
text.formatted: For AD-centered colocalization, we compared lead-variant conservation across AD-only, AD-cis, AD-trans and AD-cis-trans events using two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum tests <ref type="bibr" target="#b93">94</ref> , where the lead variant was the highest-VCP variant in each 95% CoS (or the highest-PIP variant from AD fine-mapping for AD-only loci).

text.text: To test whether conservation depended on cellular context, we fitted a linear model regressing the Zoonomia mammalian phyloP score of the lead variant on a binary indicator denoting the presence of a given cell type among the initiating (cis) cell types, the recipient (trans) cell types, or a specific initiating-recipient cell-type pair, adjusting for the leadvariant VCP and the number of distinct cell types in the colocalization event.
We evaluated whether candidate cis-trans regulatory configurations preferentially connected specific initiating and recipient cell types.
Each candidate path was represented by a proximal cis-eGene, its initiating cell type, a distal trans-eGene or trans-eProgram, and the recipient cell type in which the distal signal was observed.
Celltype-pair enrichment was calculated for each initiating-recipient cell-type pair by comparing the observed pairs to a randomized background from the null distribution.

To generate the null distribution, we randomly permuted the cell-type labels separately among cis-signals and among trans-signals, while preserving the colocalization event, the number of cis and trans signals within each event, and the marginal cell-type composition of each signal type.
This preserves the overall colocalization-level signal structure but disrupts the observed pairing between initiating and recipient cell types.
Statistical significance was calculated as the fraction of shuffled datasets with enrichment at least as large as the observed enrichment.

To obtain orthogonal support for neuron-astrocyte-specific cis-trans regulatory configurations, we compared the genes implicated by TransMap candidate paths with a published neuron-astrocyte co-culture transcriptomic dataset 51 , in which human iPSC-derived Ngn2-induced glutamatergic neurons were cultured either alone or with primary mouse cortical astrocytes.
text.formatted: To obtain orthogonal support for neuron-astrocyte-specific cis-trans regulatory configurations, we compared the genes implicated by TransMap candidate paths with a published neuron-astrocyte co-culture transcriptomic dataset <ref type="bibr" target="#b50">51</ref> , in which human iPSC-derived Ngn2-induced glutamatergic neurons were cultured either alone or with primary mouse cortical astrocytes.

text.text: This study defined 5,330 astrocyte-responsive neuronal genes as human genes differentially expressed between co-cultured and mono-cultured neurons, and 3,587 neuron-responsive astrocytic genes as mouse genes differentially expressed between co-cultured and mono-cultured astrocytes at an FDR level of 0.01.

For validation of TransMap candidate regulatory configurations, recipient-astrocytic trans-eGenes or genes assigned to recipient-astrocytic trans-ePrograms from neuron-initiated configurations were compared with neuron-responsive astrocytic genes, whereas recipient-neuronal trans-eGenes or genes assigned to recipient-neuronal trans-ePrograms from astrocyte-initiated configurations were compared with astrocyte-responsive neuronal genes.
Enrichment quantified whether TransMap recipient trans-eGenes or ePrograms were more concentrated in the corresponding co-culture-responsive gene set than expected for protein coding genes.
Statistical significance for enrichment was evaluated using a leave-one-chromosome-out jackknife.

To evaluate whether cis-neuronal and trans-glial genes from candidate cis-trans configurations showed compatible spatial proximity in human AD brain, we analyzed a published ROSMAP 10x Visium spatial transcriptomic dataset from DLPFC 52 .
text.formatted: To evaluate whether cis-neuronal and trans-glial genes from candidate cis-trans configurations showed compatible spatial proximity in human AD brain, we analyzed a published ROSMAP 10x Visium spatial transcriptomic dataset from DLPFC <ref type="bibr" target="#b51">52</ref> .

text.text: The dataset contains 32 spatial transcriptomic sections, including 4 control samples from 2 healthy donors and 28 samples from 15 donors with AD pathology.
Spots were assigned to cortical layers L1-L6 or white matter using the layer annotations provided by the original study 95 .
text.formatted: Spots were assigned to cortical layers L1-L6 or white matter using the layer annotations provided by the original study <ref type="bibr" target="#b94">95</ref> .

text.text: We grouped L1-L3 as outer cortical layer, L4-L6 as deep cortical layer and retained white matter as a separate anatomical compartment.
Gene-level spatial differential expression (DE) analysis was performed using the zero-inflated hurdle model implemented as zlm function 96 .
text.formatted: Gene-level spatial differential expression (DE) analysis was performed using the zero-inflated hurdle model implemented as zlm function <ref type="bibr" target="#b95">96</ref> .

text.text: For initiated-neuronal-recipient-glial stratum, we compared spatial expression of initiated-neuronal genes in deep cortical layer against outer cortical layer, and compared expression of recipient-glial genes in white matter against all cortical-layer spots.
Following the original study, AD samples were stratified into lower, middle and higher pathology groups, with 10, 9 and 9 samples, respectively.
DE analysis was evaluated using the full dataset and within each control or AD-pathology group.

To assess whether the greater representation of excitatory neurons influenced the inferred cross-cell-type regulatory architecture, we applied donor-stratified subsampling to generate excitatory neuron subsets containing approximately 𝑀 = 100,000, 𝑀 = 200,000and 𝑀 = 300,000 nuclei.
The complete excitatory neuron comprised 630,488 nuclei from 419 donors, accounting for 39.8% of all profiled nuclei.
For each target size 𝑀, nuclei were randomly sampled within each donor using a common sampling probability of 𝑀/630,448, subject to retaining at least 10 nuclei per donor.
This procedure maintained representation of all donors while reducing cell numbers proportionally across donors.

For each subsample, we reconstructed donor-level excitatory pseudobulk expression profiles and repeated expression preprocessing, covariate adjustment, cis-eQTL and individual gene trans-eQTL fine-mapping analysis across 1,361 LD blocks, and the corresponding cis-trans colocalization analysis using the parameters applied in the primary analysis.
Data for all other cell types were held fixed, thereby isolating the effect of excitatory neuron sampling depth.
To characterize genetic effects on brain cellular composition, we generated donor-level phenotypes for cell-type proportions in ROSMAP.
For each donor, cell-type proportions were calculated as the fraction of annotated nuclei assigned to each of six major cell types.
Each proportion phenotype was adjusted for age, sex, postmortem interval and the first 15 genotype PCs.
For each phenotype, we performed genome-wide QTL fine-mapping across 1,361 LD blocks used in the primary TransMap analyses.
Given the generally modest genetic effects on cell-type composition, candidate QTL were represented by 50% CS for downstream integration.
All association and fine-mapping settings matched those used in corresponding primary analyses.

To assess candidate molecular mediation at colocalized loci, we fitted a structural equation model (SEM) for each variant-mediator-outcome triplet, specifying genotype dosage at the lead variant with highest VCP from the corresponding 95% colocalization confidence set as the exposure, proximal cis-eGene expression as the mediator, and a distal trans-eGene or trans-eProgram phenotype as the outcome.
Molecular phenotypes were adjusted for age, sex, pmi and the top 15 genotype PC before model fitting.
We estimated the indirect association as the product of the genotype-mediator and mediator-outcome coefficients.
For assays with partially overlapping donor samples, SEM was fitted with ` lavaan` using full-information maximum likelihood under the missing-at-random assumption 53 .
text.formatted: For assays with partially overlapping donor samples, SEM was fitted with ` lavaan` using full-information maximum likelihood under the missing-at-random assumption <ref type="bibr" target="#b52">53</ref> .

text.text: We assessed uncertainty in the indirect association using 1,000 donor-level bootstrap resamples and percentile 95% confidence intervals.
Selected triplets were further examined using Bayesian SEM and missing-data sensitivity analyses.
The TransMap workflow is implemented as a modular command-line pipeline with components for phenotype construction, fine-mapping, annotation construction and colocalization.
Analyses used custom code together with established tools for sparse CCA, fine-mapping, S-LDSC and multi-phenotype colocalization.
Software versions, command-line parameters, random seeds and data-access restrictions are reported in the Code Availability, Data Availability and Reporting Summary materials.
